AWAR D 1.

Present DAR is arising out of FIR No.321/2015 registered under Section 279/304A IPC, PS M.S.
Park.

Facts as reflected in the DAR are that on 19.06.2015 at about 2.10 p.m. a DD No.23 was received in MACT Cell whereby HC Rakesh gave information that one Jitender s/o MACT No.776/2016 Page 1 Gurucharan Das has been admitted in Swami Dayanand Hospital due to sustaining injuries in accident taken place at Shahdara flyover in which tyre of the TSR no.DL-1RJ-1240 had detached.
Doctor declared the deceased having been 'brought dead'.
On the basis of same FIR No.321/2015 has been registered.

During investigation of police, statement of one eye witness namely Rinku s/o Shyam Lal and it came on the record that on the day of incident one Champion vehicle no.DL-1LL-0980 came from behind of TSR No.DL-1RJ-1240 being driven in a rash and negligent manner and hit the said TSR towards conductor side.

As a result of such impact,
front wheel of the TSR got broken, TSR hit with a divider and turned turtle with a great force and TSR driver fell on the road and crushed under the TSR.

1 2.
Upon service of notice u/s 133 M.V. Act, it revealed that offending vehicle was driven by respondent no.1 and it was owned by respondent no.2.
It is also stated that said vehicle was insured with respondent no.3/insurance company.
Respondent no.1 was charge sheeted by the police in criminal case and DAR was filed.
3. Reply to the DAR has been filed by respondent no.1 and 2 wherein entire contents of DAR have been denied.
It is stated that vehicle of respondents is not responsible for alleged accident.

4. In reply to DAR filed on behalf of respondent no.3 wherein it is pleaded that keeping in view the facts mentioned in the DAR, insurance company is entitled to take all the defences as permitted u/s 170 M.V. Act beside the defences available u/s 149(2) of M.V. Act.
It is stated that even as per the DAR, DD entry no.23 dated 19.06.2015, accident took place when the tyres of TSR suddenly came out.
In that DD there is no reference regarding involvement of any vehicle.
It is stated that notice u/s 133 M.V. Act issued for the first time on 05.07.2015, after 16 days of accident.
MACT No.776/2016 Page 2 Mechanical inspection report of the vehicle no. DL-1LL-0980 does not disclose any fresh damage on the vehicle.
As such insurance company raised doubts as to the involvement of vehicle no. DL-1LL-0980 in the accident.

5. On the basis of pleadings of parties following issues were framed by my Ld. Predecessor on 02.03.2016 :
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving vehicle bearing no.
DL-1LL-0980 on 19.06.2015 at about 12.20 pm near Flyover Shahdara, Near Pole No.56 in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and hit against TSR no.DL-1RJ- 1240 being driven by Jitender as a result Jitender sustained fatal injuries?
OPP (2)Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation, if so and for what amount?
OPP (3)Relief.
6. During the course of proceedings on behalf of petitioner two witnesses have been examined.
PW1 is Smt.Kavita (wife of deceased), PW2 is Rinku s/o Shyam Lal, eye witness to the said accident.
On behalf of respondent no.3, one witness R3W1 Rishabh Saboo (AR of respondent no.3) has been examined.
7. I have heard submissions of Ms.Sonia Chauhan, ld. Counsel for petitioner.
I have also heard the submissions of Sh.Ashish Chauhan, ld counsel for insurance company and also gone through the written submissions.
Issue No.1 8.
It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the MACT No.776/2016 Page 3 touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.

Holistic view is to be taken while Kavita vs Beyas Singh on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112034404/
2 dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others. (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
9.

sentences.text: In this case as is evident from the perusal of the DAR on 19.06.2015 when accident took place information received to MACT Cell from PS M.S. Park, wherein it was mentioned that the driver of the TSR died due to detachment of tyre of the TSR and driver received injuries.

It is on the basis of such information local police station registered the FIR no.321/2015, when there was no details regarding the manner in which accident has taken place as that stage no eye witness was found either at the place of accident or even in hospital.

Perusal of the report u/s 173 Cr.PC annexed with the DAR mentions that later during the investigation an eye witness Rinku met with the police and informed the manner in which accident took place as well as referred to involvement of vehicle no.
DL- 1LL-0980 in the accident.
On the basis of such information received, notice u/s 133 M.V. Act dated 05.07.2015 was served to registered owner of that vehicle i.e. Umesh Chand.
In pursuance to that wife of Umesh Chand appeared and disclosed the name of the respondent no.1 being driver of the offending vehicle.
Driver also appeared and later offending vehicle was seized by the investigating officer.

10. It is in view of such factual background counsel for the MACT No.776/2016 Page 4 Insurance company has submitted that offending vehicle has been falsely implicated because the DD entry no.23 dated 19.06.2015 regarding the unfortunate accident does not mention regarding involvement of vehicle no. DL-1LL-0980.
It is submitted that there is an inordinate delay in introduction of the above said vehicle shown to be involved in the accident.
It is submitted that statement and evidence of so called eye witness Rinku (PW2) is also unworthy of any reliance because of inherent contradictions.
It is submitted that version of accident also does not get corroboration from mechanical inspection.

Counsel for the insurance relied upon the judgments in Veerappa and ors.
vs. Siddappa and ors.
(MFA No.8488/2004 decided on 03.11.2000), United India Insurance Company Limited and ors. vs. Ninganna and ors.

Counsel for the petitioner submitted that evidence of eye witness is cogent and sufficient to rely upon regarding the manner in which accident took place as well as to prove rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 which resulted in causing of accident due to detachment of tyre of TSR and causing of fatal injuries to deceased.
12. Having considered the submissions, at the outset it be noted that information regarding the accident has been received by DD No.23 dated 19.06.2015 from MACT Cell.
No doubt in that DD it is mentioned that accident had occurred on account of detachment of the tyre of TSR of the deceased resulting in causing of fatal injuries to deceased.

But as it is known to all that DD or FIR Kavita vs Beyas Singh on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112034404/
3 even cannot be encyclopedia therefore MACT No.776/2016 Page 5 contents of DD recorded at that stage cannot be taken to be the only truth of the matter.

sentences.text:
Perusal of the DAR shows that later during the investigation eye witness met the IO and gave the account of the accident giving details of involvement of offending vehicle no. DL-1LL-0980.
13.
That eye witness whose statement was recorded by the police, has been examined in this case as PW2.
PW2 in his deposition has stated that on 19.06.2015 he was going on his motorcycle DL-5S-BW-4606 in a normal speed towards Seelampur from Dilshad Garden.

When he was going on Shahdara flyover, TSR No.DL-1RJ-1240 was going ahead of him and in the meantime a Champion vehicle no. DL-1LL-0980 came from behind, overtook motorcycle of PW2 in a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and hit TSR No.DL-1RJ-1240 with a great force from conductor side.
As a result of forceful impact the front wheel of the TSR broke down and TSR turned turtle due to which driver of the TSR fell down on the road and crushed under the TSR.
14. On the above details of the accident, PW2 was cross examined in length.
Counsel for the insurance raised certain aspects of the cross examination to submit that evidence of PW2 is unworthy of reliance.

However at the outset it be noted that in proceedings of accident claims,
evidence is required to be assessed broadly, to conclude regarding prove of a fact by preponderance of probabilities.
Therefore evidence of eye witness cannot be minutely examined, as may be required in a criminal case for accident.
Moreover evidence of PW2 in totality, appears to be inspiring as PW2 in cross examination stated that he saw the accident from the distance of about 100 feet.
PW2 stated that offending vehicle hit the vehicle (TSR of deceased) from left side.

He stated that after the accident he remained at the spot for 10-15 minutes and when two three persons gathered at the spot MACT No.776/2016 Page 6 and one scooty driver removed the deceased from the spot of accident to the hospital.
15. Nothing came in the cross examination to render the evidence of PW2 regarding the manner in which accident has taken place, to be unbelievable.
No doubt in cross examination witness stated that he came to know about the death of the deceased in that accident in newspaper, after 10/12 days of the accident.
PW2 also stated that he saw the offending vehicle no. DL-1LL-0980 and noted down on some paper but lost with the theft of his vehicle.
Therefore he could not hand over the slip on which he noted the number, to police.
Such version is only with regard to recording of number of offending vehicle.
Such version of PW2 though appears to be improbable but still cannot be considered to be impossible in certain situations.

Different persons behave differently in similar situations, therefore only on this aspect entire evidence of PW2 cannot be brushed aside, more particularly when his statement was recorded by the police during the investigation.

On the basis of information so provided by PW2, police served the notice u/s 133 M.V. Act, wherein the driver and wife of registered owner admitted the involvement of offending vehicle no. DL- 1LL-0980.
16.
Investigating Officer verified all the facts at the very outset and prepared the site plan which also indicate involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.
Thus, the evidence of PW2 gets corroboration from police documents and conclusion of IO in the investigation.

Counsel for the insurance company relied upon judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in United India Insurance vs. Ninganna (supra), that judgment however is distinguishable in the facts as in para 10 Hon'ble Court noted that there was inordinate delay in filing MACT No.776/2016 Page 7 complaint about the alleged road side accident as well as discrepancy in medical record.
Therefore it was concluded that there were certain manipulations.
In the present case there was no delay in recording the details of accident and registration of FIR.
However police later recorded the statement of eye witness in the investigation.

Similarly judgment of Karnataka High Court in Bajaj Allianz General Insurance vs. B.C. Kumar (supra) is also distinguishable because in that case Tribunal excessively relied upon pleading of guilt by the driver of the alleged vehicle in criminal case.

sentences.text: It is in that context Hon'ble High Court held that when there was no evidence on the record of Claim Tribunal, evidence of plea of guilt should not have been relied upon for deciding the question of compensation.

Similarly another judgment of Veerappa and others (supra) was distinguishable in facts because in that case Hon'ble High Court held that mere admission of owner of the vehicle has limited legal value, Tribunal has to decide the question of compensation on the basis of cogent and specific evidence regarding involvement, rash and negligent driving and other aspects.

Another judgment of Apex Court in Safiq Ahmad's case (supra) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has formed SIT.
18.
There is no denial to the fact that in many cases there is manipulation, fraudulent activities are being done to make out a case and to raise a false claim of compensation.
However all cases cannot be taken with negative mindset.
Even as per the guidelines laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court, there must be material on the record to conclude regarding fraudulent activities or manipulations.

In the present case for the reasons as discussed above, I find that there is sufficient material record showing involvement of offending vehicle as well as the rash and negligent driving of the same by respondent no.1 which resulted in detachment of tyre of the MACT No.776/2016 Page 8 TSR due to forceful impact and consequent fatal injuries suffered by the deceased.
Issue accordingly decided in favour of petitioner.
Issue No.2 19.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 20.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Jitender.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

sentences.text: Further, the guidelines have been reiterated by the Constitution Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.

sentences.text:
Decided on 31.10.2017,
laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases.

The relevant Kavita vs Beyas Singh on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112034404/
5 paras of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"18.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
MACT No.776/2016 Page 10 Step-3 (Actual Calculation)
The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand) when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.

Kavita vs Beyas Singh on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112034404/
6 Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."
21.
Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:-

PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age of deceased :
22.
Wife of deceased Ms.Kavita has appeared as PW1 and testified that her husband met with a road accident on 19.06.2015 and died on the same day.
PW1 further testifies that at the time of accident age of her husband was 44 years as his date of birth is 01.06.1971.
PW1 proved death certificate, DL and badge of deceased as Ex.PW1/1 and Ex.PW1/2.
This aspect of the evidence of PW1 is not disputed, moreover election identity card of deceased being part of DAR proves the age of the deceased to be 44 years at the time of his death in accident.
Assessment of Income of deceased :
23. PW1 in her deposition stated that her husband was driving own TSR and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
PW1 proved DL and MACT No.776/2016 Page 11 badge of the deceased beside registration certificate of TSR Ex.PW1/2 and Ex.PW1/3 respectively.

24. Having considered the evidence, although it is established on the record that deceased was driving TSR, however his income as claimed to be Rs.25,000/- has not been proved by any documentary evidence.
In such circumstance deceased being driver of TSR, his income is assessed to be at parity with minimum wages of a skilled worker in Delhi which is Rs.11,154/- per month.

Application of Multiplier:
25.
As held above, deceased was 44 years of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.

The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the Kavita vs Beyas Singh on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112034404/
7 multiplier.

Age group between 66 and above 26.
In view of the above, multiplier of 14 has to be applied MACT No.776/2016 Page 12 against the age bracket of 41 to 45 years to determine the compensation.

Future Prospects:
27.

Regarding future prospects ld. counsel for insurance company submitted that since the income of the deceased and nature of occupation has not been duly proved,
therefore no amount may be fixed for future prospects.
Reliance has been placed in judgment of Maharashtra High Court in New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt.Alpa Rajesh Shah (MANU/MH/1693/2013).

sentences.text: 28. Having considered such submissions, first of all the occupation of deceased being TSR driver is well proved on the record.
Only aspect, on which there was no sufficient evidence was about exact income of the deceased at the time of accident.
This Tribunal therefore has already assessed the income of the deceased at parity with minimum wages of skilled worker.

There is no reason for not providing future prospects to the deceased in terms of ratio laid down in Sarla Verma's case (supra)
and Pranay Sethi's case (supra).

Relevant parts of judgment in case of Pranay Sethi (supra) reads as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

(iv) In case, the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to Kavita vs Beyas Singh on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112034404/
8 50 years MACT No.776/2016 Page 13 and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

The established income means the income minus the tax component."
29.

Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 44 years, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 25% of the income of deceased (between the age of 40 to 50 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.
Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses:
30. After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
 Deductions out of earning of the Number of  deceased dependents  Where dependent is 1 Half  Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd  members is 2 to 3  Where the number of dependent family 1/4th  members is 4 to 6  Where the number of dependent family 1/5th  members exceeds 6 (six)
31.

sentences.text: Instant claim petition has been filed by only one petitioner i.e. widow of deceased.
Since, the deceased was survived by only one dependent, half of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his MACT No.776/2016 Page 14 personal living expenses.

NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
32.

In case of Pranay Sethi (Supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.48,000/-,
18,000/- and Rs.18,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.

33. Considering the aforementioned factors, the total compensation is calculated as under:

INTEREST ON AWARD 35.
Petitioner shall also be entitled to interest @ 8% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
LIABILITY 36.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
It is matter of record that the vehicle in question was duly insured with respondent no.3/insurance company.
Therefore the amount of compensation is payable by respondent no.3/ insurance company to the petitioner.
Relief 37.

This Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.12,55,170/- to the petitioner along with interest @
8% per annum from the date of filing of petition till realization to be paid by respondent no.3/insurance company.
Amount of interim award, if any, be deducted from the compensation amount along with the waiver of interest, if any, as directed by the Tribunal during the pendency of this case.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the MACT No.776/2016 Page 3 touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others. (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
9.
Such version is only with regard to recording of number of offending vehicle.
Different persons behave differently in similar situations, therefore only on this aspect entire evidence of PW2 cannot be brushed aside, more particularly when his statement was recorded by the police during the investigation.
On the basis of information so provided by PW2, police served the notice u/s 133 M.V. Act, wherein the driver and wife of registered owner admitted the involvement of offending vehicle no. DL- 1LL-0980.
16.
Thus, the evidence of PW2 gets corroboration from police documents and conclusion of IO in the investigation.
Counsel for the insurance company relied upon judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in United India Insurance vs. Ninganna (supra), that judgment however is distinguishable in the facts as in para 10 Hon'ble Court noted that there was inordinate delay in filing MACT No.776/2016 Page 7 complaint about the alleged road side accident as well as discrepancy in medical record.
In the present case there was no delay in recording the details of accident and registration of FIR.
However police later recorded the statement of eye witness in the investigation.
There is no denial to the fact that in many cases there is manipulation, fraudulent activities are being done to make out a case and to raise a false claim of compensation.
Even as per the guidelines laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court, there must be material on the record to conclude regarding fraudulent activities or manipulations.
In the present case for the reasons as discussed above, I find that there is sufficient material record showing involvement of offending vehicle as well as the rash and negligent driving of the same by respondent no.1 which resulted in detachment of tyre of the MACT No.776/2016 Page 8 TSR due to forceful impact and consequent fatal injuries suffered by the deceased.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
This aspect of the evidence of PW1 is not disputed, moreover election identity card of deceased being part of DAR proves the age of the deceased to be 44 years at the time of his death in accident.
In such circumstance deceased being driver of TSR, his income is assessed to be at parity with minimum wages of a skilled worker in Delhi which is Rs.11,154/- per month.
As held above, deceased was 44 years of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the Kavita vs Beyas Singh on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112034404/
7 multiplier.
Reliance has been placed in judgment of Maharashtra High Court in New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt.Alpa Rajesh Shah (MANU/MH/1693/2013).
This Tribunal therefore has already assessed the income of the deceased at parity with minimum wages of skilled worker.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
29.
Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 44 years, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 25% of the income of deceased (between the age of 40 to 50 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
 Deductions out of earning of the Number of  deceased dependents  Where dependent is 1 Half  Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd  members is 2 to 3  Where the number of dependent family 1/4th  members is 4 to 6  Where the number of dependent family 1/5th  members exceeds 6 (six)
